name: q-lint
description: q/kdb+ for VS Code: linting, Quick Fixes, navigation and help from the source, and connections to q processes to run code on.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Linting, Quick Fixes, navigation and colouring work in Restricted Mode: the linter reads q and never runs it. The settings that name a program, a command or the language server's arguments, the read-only guard's and the drill-down queries, are taken from your user settings only, the workspace's .env is not given to q, q binaries in the workspace are not offered, and git is not run in it.

q-lint.enable.markdownDescription: Run the q-lint language server. Off, it starts no server: no diagnostics, Quick Fixes, formatting, navigation or semantic colouring. The grammar's colouring, processes, queries, the Process Explorer, notebooks and the agent tool stay.

q-lint.serverPath.markdownDescription: Path to the `qlinter` binary; a leading `~` is your home directory. Left empty, the extension uses the server it was packaged with, and falls back to `qlinter` on `PATH` when it was packaged without one or that one will not run. Set, it always wins.

q-lint.serverArgs.markdownDescription: Extra command-line arguments for `qlinter --lsp`, after the ones the other settings produce - for example `["--isolated"]` or `["--extend-select", "QS001"]`. Flags given here keep their command-line meaning, so unlike `#q-lint.lint.select#` they can widen what the repository's configuration selects.

q-lint.profile.markdownDescription: Which rules to run. Set here, it overrides `profile` in a repository's `qlinter.toml`; left unset, the repository's configuration decides, and `style` applies where there is none. `style` reports what q refuses and what q runs but is almost certainly a mistake. `general` keeps only what q itself rejects; `styleq` adds the conventions of published q style guides; `uqf` adds one repository's house conventions on top of those.

q-lint.configFile.markdownDescription: A configuration file to use for every document instead of the nearest `.qlinter.toml`, `qlinter.toml` or `pyproject.toml` `[tool.qlinter]` (the server's `--config`). Relative to the first workspace folder; a leading `~` is your home directory. Empty: the nearest one governs each file, as on the command line and in CI.

q-lint.lint.select.markdownDescription: Show only these rules, among those the configuration already turns on. Rule codes or prefixes, as `qlinter --rules` lists them. It narrows and never widens: a rule the repository's configuration leaves off stays off. Empty: no narrowing.

q-lint.lint.ignore.markdownDescription: Hide these rules in the editor. Rule codes or prefixes, as `qlinter --rules` lists them. Applied after the configuration, so it can only hide; the repository's configuration, which CI reads, is unchanged.

enumDescriptions: Lint the buffer on every change.
Lint when the file is opened and saved. Quick Fixes match the last saved lint, so they appear again after a save.

q-lint.lint.workspaceScope.enable.markdownDescription: Show problems for every `.q` file the workspace index reads, not only the open ones: each is read from disk and linted while the editor is otherwise idle, at most 5,000 of them, and again when it changes on disk, or when a save or a change on disk changes what the workspace defines. Files `#q-lint.workspaceIndex.exclude#` or the configuration's `exclude` skip are not linted, and with `#q-lint.workspaceIndex.enable#` off there are none. Off, only open files show problems.

q-lint.lint.severity.markdownDescription: The severity the editor shows, by rule code or prefix; the longest that names a rule decides. For example `{"QS": "hint", "QE": "error"}`. Display only: what is reported does not change.

q-lint.fixes.unsafe.markdownDescription: Offer the editor-only Quick Fixes too: those `qlinter --fix` applies only with `--unsafe-fixes`, because they can change what a working program does or guess at what was meant. Off, only the fixes `qlinter --fix` applies are offered.

q-lint.format.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Format Document**, which applies the fixes `qlinter --fix` applies and nothing else. Off, q-lint does not register as a formatter.

q-lint.semanticTokens.enable.markdownDescription: Colour functions where they are called and parameters where they are read, on top of the grammar's colouring. Off, only the grammar colours.

q-lint.navigation.enable.markdownDescription: Offer the outline, workspace symbols, **Go to Definition**, **Find All References**, occurrence highlights, **Rename Symbol** for a local or a global across the workspace - all read from the source, never by running it. Off, q-lint announces none of them: turn it off when another q extension already navigates and both would answer.

q-lint.help.enable.markdownDescription: Show a hover and signature help: for a name the workspace defines, its parameters, the comment above its definition and its file; for a word of q itself, how it is written and what it gives. Read from the source and a built-in catalogue, never from a running q. Off, q-lint announces neither.

q-lint.completion.enable.markdownDescription: Complete names as you type: a lambda's parameters and locals, the names the workspace's `.q` files define, and q's own words. It knows no table's columns and nothing only a running process holds. Off by default, because an editor that is told a server completes stops offering the words already in the file.

q-lint.callHierarchy.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Show Call Hierarchy** on a global function: the definitions and files that name it, and the workspace functions its own definition names. Read from the source, never by running it, so a name used as a value counts as a call and a call made through a string is not seen. Off, q-lint does not announce it.

q-lint.graph.enable.markdownDescription: Offer the **q Dependencies** view - the files the active q file depends on and those depending on it - and **q-lint: List Affected Tests**, the test files that reach a q file changed against git HEAD. Both are what `qlinter analyze graph` prints. Off, the server answers neither and the view is hidden.

q-lint.rename.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Rename Symbol** (F2): a lambda's parameter or local within its lambda, and a global in every workspace file that names it, under the `\d` each is written in. Needs `q-lint.navigation.enable`. Off, q-lint does not announce renaming, and the rest of navigation stays.

q-lint.inlayHints.enable.markdownDescription: Show parameter names at the arguments of a bracketed call to a workspace function - `f[a: 1; b: 2]` drawn over `f[1;2]` - for a function whose definitions all declare the same signature. Read from the source, never from a running q. VS Code's own `editor.inlayHints.enabled` hides them too, or shows them only while a key is held. Off, q-lint announces none.

q-lint.codeLens.enable.markdownDescription: Show **Run** above each function a statement at column 0 defines, and **Run test** above one named `test_*` (or qUnit's `testName`). Run sends the definition to the connected process - under the `\d` it is written in - as a query from the editor would be sent; Run test sends it and then calls it with no argument. Off, q-lint announces no lenses.

q-lint.documentLinks.enable.markdownDescription: Make the path of each load - `\l lib/x.q`, `system "l lib/x.q"` or a file symbol `` `:lib/x.q `` - a link: Ctrl/Cmd+click opens the file, found against the workspace folder and then the loading file's own directory and each one above it, as **Go to Definition** on the path finds it. Off, q-lint announces no links.

q-lint.generateQdoc.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Generate qDoc for f** in the lightbulb and **Refactor...** menu inside a function a statement at column 0 defines: it writes a `/ @param` line for each parameter and a `/ @return` line directly above the definition, for the descriptions to be typed after. Not offered where the comment above already has an `@param` or `@return`. Off, q-lint offers no such action.

q-lint.extractFunction.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Extract function** in the lightbulb and **Refactor...** menu over a selection: it becomes a lambda defined above the top-level statement it is in, taking the parameters and locals it reads, and the selection a call to it. Only a selection q reads as one value is rewritten; **Refactor...** says why another is refused. Off, q-lint offers no such action.

q-lint.autoLoad.enable.markdownDescription: When completing a name that one other workspace file defines, and nothing this file loads or is loaded with defines, accepting it also writes the `\l` that loads that file: after the file's last load above the cursor, keeping their order. Never a second load of a file already reached, and nothing for a name two files define. Needs `#q-lint.completion.enable#`. Off by default: accepting a name then writes a line elsewhere in the file.

q-lint.referenceLens.enable.markdownDescription: Show **N references** above each function a statement at column 0 defines: the places the workspace's `.q` files read it, as **Find All References** lists them without the assignments. Click it to see them. Read from the source, never from a running q. Off, q-lint shows no such lens.

q-lint.inferredTypes.enable.markdownDescription: Show a lambda local's type on hover and as an inlay hint after its value (`a:1 2 3 long list`), only where every assignment of it is a literal of the same type, so the type is the one q's `type` gives. An expression, a parameter or an amend shows nothing rather than a guess. Off, q-lint shows neither.

q-lint.suppressions.enable.markdownDescription: Offer the Quick Fixes that accept a finding instead of fixing it: **Suppress CODE on this line**, which writes `/ noqa: CODE` after its line, and **Suppress CODE in this file**, which writes `/ qlinter: noqa: CODE` at the top of the file or adds the code to the one there. Off, q-lint offers neither.

q-lint.organiseLoads.enable.markdownDescription: Answer **Organize Imports** (and `source.organizeImports` in `editor.codeActionsOnSave`) with **Organise loads**: in each run of consecutive `\l` lines, a path loaded twice is loaded once and the rest are sorted, absolute paths first, then relative ones. A run that loads anything but a `.q` or `.k` file is left alone. Off, q-lint offers no such action and **q-lint: Organise Loads** is hidden.

q-lint.performanceLints.enable.markdownDescription: Report the performance rules, `QV`: a where phrase that constrains the partition column after another, `each` over an atomic builtin such as `abs`, and `r:r,x` in a loop. Off, they are hidden as `#q-lint.lint.ignore#` would hide them.

q-lint.formatChangedLines.enable.markdownDescription: On saving a q file in a git repository, apply the safe fixes **Format Document** makes, for the findings on the lines changed against `HEAD` only. Outside git nothing is changed. Off by default: it edits the file at every save. Off, nothing listens and **q-lint: Format Changed Lines** is hidden.

q-lint.qsqlLayout.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Lay out qSQL query on aligned lines** in the lightbulb and **Refactor...** menu inside a `select`, `exec`, `update` or `delete`: each clause on its own line, `by`, `from` and `where` right-aligned under the first word, and the columns or constraints one per line where they do not fit in `#q-lint.qsqlLayout.lineLength#`. Only blanks change, and a query where a new line could change what q reads (a comment in it, say) is left alone. Off, q-lint offers no such action, and Format Document does not lay queries out.

q-lint.qsqlLayout.onFormat.markdownDescription: Have **Format Document** also lay out every qSQL query longer than `#q-lint.qsqlLayout.lineLength#`, after the safe fixes. Off by default, so formatting (and a format on save) keeps to the safe fixes. Needs `#q-lint.qsqlLayout.enable#`.

q-lint.qsqlLayout.lineLength.markdownDescription: The line length a qSQL query is laid out to: Format Document lays out a query longer than this, and a clause's columns or constraints go one per line when they would not fit.

q-lint.workspaceIndex.enable.markdownDescription: Read every `.q` file in the workspace at startup, never running it, so a name another file defines is not reported as undefined and is coloured as a function. Off, only open files are indexed.

q-lint.workspaceIndex.exclude.markdownDescription: Globs, relative to the workspace folder, of files and directories the workspace index does not read - for example `["vendor/**", "**/generated/**"]`. An open file is still linted and indexed. Whatever the configuration's `exclude` skips - by default `.git`, `.venv`, `node_modules`, `__pycache__`, `build`, `dist` and `target` - is skipped too, as `qlinter .` skips it.

q-lint.trace.server.description: Log the traffic between VS Code and the server, for debugging the integration itself.

q-lint.functionalForm.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Rewrite qSQL query in functional form** inside a `select`, `exec`, `update` or `delete`, and **Rewrite functional form as qSQL** inside a `?[t;c;b;a]` or `![t;c;b;a]`, in the lightbulb and **Refactor...** menu and as palette commands. Each column, constraint and grouping is written as the parse tree q's `parse` gives; what the rewrite cannot read (an adverb, a projection, `select[n]`) is refused with the reason. Off, the server offers neither and the commands are hidden.

q-lint.qsqlExplain.enable.markdownDescription: Say a qSQL query in words on hover over its `select`, `exec`, `update` or `delete` (or a functional form's `?`/`!`): what it reads, which rows it keeps, how it groups them and what it returns. Deterministic and offline. Also **q-lint: Explain qSQL Query**. Off, the hover leaves the words out and the command is hidden.

q-lint.versionCheck.enable.markdownDescription: Report the QK rules: what does not run on the q release a folder's configuration names in `target-version` (`3.6`, `4.0`, `4.1` or `kdbx`). Without a `target-version` they report nothing. Off, they are hidden as `#q-lint.lint.ignore#` would.

q-lint.baseline.enable.markdownDescription: Hide the findings in the lint baseline a folder's configuration names (`baseline = "qlinter-baseline.json"`), so only new findings show; and offer **q-lint: Write Lint Baseline**. Off, every finding is shown and the command is hidden.

q-lint.typeLints.enable.markdownDescription: Report the lints from inferred types (style profile): a local that is always a symbol compared with a string or number (QT033), lists of different types joined (QT034), arithmetic on a local that is always a symbol (QT035). Off, they are hidden as `#q-lint.lint.ignore#` would.

q-lint.selectionRange.enable.markdownDescription: Grow **Expand Selection** by q's structure: the token, then each bracket around it - the `;`-separated item, the contents, the bracket, a call with its name - then the top-level statement. Read from the source, never from a running q. Off, q-lint announces none and VS Code's own word-and-bracket selection is used.

q-lint.relatedInformation.enable.markdownDescription: Link a problem that points at a second place to that place, under the problem in the Problems panel and its hover: the first of two parameters of one name (QF008), the first of two columns of one name (QB019), the result column a `by` group repeats (QB021). Off, the problems are shown alone.

q-lint.crossFileRefresh.enable.markdownDescription: Redraw the code lenses and inlay hints of every open q file when another file's definitions change - a parameter renamed, a function added - and the reference counts when the names a file reads change. Off, a file's lenses and hints are redrawn only when it is edited itself.

q-lint.renameLoads.enable.markdownDescription: When a `.q` or `.k` file or a folder is renamed or moved in the Explorer, rewrite the `\l` paths (and `system "l ..."` and `` `:file.q `` paths) that name it - or anything under the folder - so they still reach it, each from the base it was written against: the workspace folder, or the loading file's own directory. A moved file's own loads are rewritten too. Off, a rename changes no file.

q-lint.loadPathCompletion.enable.markdownDescription: Complete the folders and `.q`/`.k` scripts after `\l `, from the file's own directory and the workspace folder; a `/` lists the next folder's. Only a `\l` line is answered unless `#q-lint.completion.enable#` is on too, so VS Code's word suggestions are kept everywhere else. Off, nothing is completed after `\l`.

q-lint.output.consoleSize.markdownDescription: Height and width, in characters, a query's result is formatted to (`.Q.S` on the process). A larger result is cut there, by the process, before it is sent.

q-lint.output.autoClear.markdownDescription: Clear the **q-lint: query** output before each result.

q-lint.output.includeQuery.markdownDescription: Show the code that was run above its result.

q-lint.output.ignoreNullReturn.markdownDescription: Show nothing for a query whose value is `::`, such as an assignment ending in `;`.

enumDescriptions: Show every result in the **q-lint: query** output, as q formats it.
Show a table, dictionary or list in the **q-lint: result** panel as a table you can sort, filter and copy as CSV. Anything else goes to the output.
Show a table, dictionary or list in the **q-lint: result** panel as a chart of its numeric columns. Anything else goes to the output.
q-lint.query.mode.markdownDescription: Where a query's result is shown. **q-lint: Switch Query Mode** changes it.

q-lint.query.gridLimit.markdownDescription: The most rows of a result the process sends to the grid or chart. The panel says when a result was cut, and how many rows it had.

q-lint.query.gridDecimals.markdownDescription: Decimal places the grid shows a float or real to, and copies as CSV. `-1`: as the process writes it, to its `\P` precision.

enumDescriptions: Open the **q-lint: result** panel beside the editor.
Show the result in the **q Results** view in the bottom panel, beside the terminal and the output.
q-lint.query.resultsLocation.markdownDescription: Where a grid or chart result is shown: beside the editor, or in the **q Results** view in the bottom panel.

q-lint.query.resultHistory.markdownDescription: How many grid or chart results the result panel keeps as tabs. **q-lint: Show Result from History** picks one too.

q-lint.results.history.enable.markdownDescription: Keep the last `q-lint.query.resultHistory` results as tabs in the result panel, and offer **q-lint: Show Result from History**.

q-lint.results.diff.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Compare** in the result panel, and **q-lint: Compare Result with Previous Run**: mark what changed since the previous run of the same query. Off, no previous result is kept.

q-lint.results.statistics.enable.markdownDescription: Offer the result panel's **Stats** view, and **q-lint: Show Column Statistics**: each column's count, nulls, distinct values, min, max and mean.

q-lint.results.heatmap.enable.markdownDescription: Offer the grid's **Heatmap** button, and **q-lint: Toggle Result Heatmap**. Off, no column is coloured, whatever `q-lint.query.gridHeatmap` says.

q-lint.results.tree.enable.markdownDescription: Offer the result panel's **Tree** view of a dictionary or a nested list, and **q-lint: Show Result as Tree**. Off, the process is not asked for the tree.

q-lint.results.export.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Export as...** in the result panel, **q-lint: Export Results As...** and **q-lint: Copy Results As...**: the rows shown as Excel, Parquet, JSON, a Markdown table, a q expression that rebuilds the table, or an HTML page. Export to CSV is always offered.

q-lint.results.paging.enable.markdownDescription: Page through a result cut at `q-lint.query.gridLimit`: the process keeps the whole result as `.qlint.held`, and the grid asks it for the next `gridLimit` rows as it scrolls to the end, up to 1,000,000 rows. Off by default, because it defines `.qlint.held` on the process and holds the result there until the next grid query while paging is on (`.qlint.held:()` frees it). Never on a process tagged `prod`, and never in direct evaluation (unwrapped).

q-lint.results.pivot.enable.markdownDescription: Offer the result panel's **Pivot** view, and **q-lint: Show Result as Pivot**: rows by one column, columns by another, and the count, sum, average, min or max of a third.

q-lint.results.charts.enable.markdownDescription: Offer the area, step and candle charts, a second y axis, the chart's **Save PNG** and **Save SVG** buttons, and **q-lint: Save Result Chart as Image**. Off, the chart offers line, bar, scatter and histogram.

q-lint.results.drilldown.enable.markdownDescription: Offer the drill-down queries of `q-lint.results.drilldownTemplates` on a grid cell: double-click it, or right-click it and choose **Drill Down from Cell**. The query picked runs on the process the result came from, after a confirmation on a production one.

label.description: What the pick shows. The query, when there is no label.

query.description: The q to run. {{value}} is the cell's value as q, {{column}} its column's name as a symbol, {{row.name}} the value of column name in the same row.

columns.description: The columns it is offered for. Every column when left out.

q-lint.results.drilldownTemplates.markdownDescription: Follow-up queries a grid cell offers. In `query`, `{{value}}` is the cell's value as a q literal (`` `AAPL ``, `2024.01.02`, `0Nj`), `{{column}}` its column's name as a symbol, and `{{row.name}}` the value of column `name` in the same row. For example `{"label": "Trades", "query": "select from trade where date={{row.date}}, sym={{value}}", "columns": ["sym"]}`.

q-lint.results.wrangler.enable.markdownDescription: Offer the **Data Wrangler**: **q-lint: Wrangle Result...**, and **Wrangle Column...** on a grid column header's menu. Filter, sort, rename, cast and drop, each step recorded as q (`select ... where`, `xasc`, `xcol`, `update`, `delete`) and run over the result's query on its process, in the grid; **Show steps as q** opens them in an editor. Only a result of a single expression can be wrangled.

q-lint.results.editCells.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Edit Cell...** on a grid cell's menu: it writes the `update` that sets the cell in the table the result came from (`` update c:v from `t where ... ``), shows it, and sends it only when you choose **Run**, through the read-only guard. Off, the menu item is hidden and nothing is written or sent.

q-lint.results.columnFormats.enable.markdownDescription: Format a grid column by the suffix its name ends in (#1012): `_PCT` a fraction as a percent, `_BPS` in basis points, `_CCY` an amount with thousands separated and two decimals, `_NUM` thousands separated (each may end in a digit, the decimals: `_PCT1`), `_BG` and `_FG` a colour taken from the value for the column the rest of the name names (or the row), `_CODE` monospace, `_BAR` a data bar. The header shows the name without its suffix, which stays in its tooltip. Off, every column is shown as q writes it.

q-lint.results.conditionalFormats.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Add Conditional Format...** and **Clear Conditional Formats** on a grid column header's menu (#1013): a comparison (`>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`, `=`, `<>`, top or bottom N, contains) against a value, and a background, a text colour or bold. Rules are kept per result tab and with the saved query the result came from, and go into the Excel export (as Excel's own conditional formatting) and the HTML export. Off, the items are hidden and no rule is drawn or exported.

q-lint.results.cellCharts.enable.markdownDescription: Draw a column of numeric lists as sparklines, and offer **Toggle Data Bar** (on a numeric column) and **Toggle Sparkline** (on a column of numeric lists) on a grid column header's menu (#1014). A data bar is scaled to the column's range, from zero. Off, every cell is text.

q-lint.results.columnLayout.enable.markdownDescription: Remember the grid's column layout (#1015): drag a header to move its column or its right edge to resize it, and **Hide Column**, **Freeze Columns up to Here** and **Unfreeze Columns** on a header's menu, with **Show Hidden Result Columns** and **Reset Result Column Layout** in the palette. Kept per result tab, for the next run of the same code, and with the saved query the result came from, restored when it runs again. Off, the grid draws every column in its order, nothing is kept.

q-lint.results.depthChart.enable.markdownDescription: Offer a **Depth** chart for an order book (#1016): bid and ask price and size columns by level (`bidPx`, `bidSize`, `askPx`, `askSize`, ...), as lists in a row, or `side`, `price` and `size` columns. Cumulative size either side of the mid, chosen by itself when the columns fit. Off, it is not offered.

q-lint.results.mapChart.enable.markdownDescription: Offer a **Map** chart for a result with latitude and longitude columns (#1017): the rows as points on a plain outline of the world, bundled with the extension, sized and coloured by optional columns. Nothing is fetched. Off, it is not offered.

q-lint.results.linkedCharts.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Linked panes** (#1018): each series in its own pane on one x axis; a crosshair reads every series at the cursor, a drag zooms every pane, a double-click shows all again. Off, it is not offered.

q-lint.results.chartPresets.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Save with Query** on the chart, **Save Result Chart with Query** and **Forget Result Chart Preset** (#1019), and a colour for each series: the chart's kind, series, right axis, bins, colours and map columns are kept with the saved query, and running it again draws the same chart. Off, nothing is kept and a kept chart is not drawn.

q-lint.results.correlation.enable.markdownDescription: Offer the **Correlation** view and **Show Result Correlation Matrix** (#1020): the Pearson correlation of every pair of numeric columns over the rows shown, computed here, as a heatmap and a list of pairs. Off, it is not offered.

q-lint.results.sendResult.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Send to...** on the result, **Send Result to Notebook** and **Append Result to Markdown Report...** (#1021): the query, the rows shown as a Markdown table and, if you like, the chart as an image, inserted into a q notebook as a Markdown cell or added to the end of a Markdown file, after showing what it will write. Off, they are hidden and nothing is written.

q-lint.results.accessibleGrid.enable.markdownDescription: Expose the result grid to screen readers (#1187): a `grid` with its whole row and column counts though only the rows in view are drawn, each row's index among them, the column names as column headers, and one tab stop that the arrow keys move from cell to cell - Home and End to a row's ends, Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End to the grid's, Page Up and Page Down a page, scrolling as they go; Enter or Space on a header still sorts. Off, the grid is a plain table and every header is a tab stop.

q-lint.results.announce.enable.markdownDescription: Announce a query's outcome to a screen reader (#1188), politely, without moving the focus: `1,000 rows in 12 ms` when the result panel shows a result, and in the Interactive Window and the q REPL how many lines a run answered and how long it took, or its error. Off, nothing is announced and the live region is not in the page.

q-lint.query.gridHeatmap.markdownDescription: Colour the grid's numeric columns by value, in the theme's chart colours: blue from the least to the greatest, or, for a column either side of zero, blue above it and red below. **q-lint: Toggle Result Heatmap** and the grid's **Heatmap** button change it.

q-lint.query.unwrapped.markdownDescription: Evaluate directly: send a query as a plain string, statement by statement, for a gateway that refuses a lambda, instead of in the lambda q-lint runs it with. The result is whatever the process returns, formatted by q-lint rather than the process, so it is close to q's console but not exact; an error has no backtrace; `reval` is not applied; and features that need q-lint's lambda (benchmark, line timings, async queries...) refuse. It is the default for every process: one whose `evaluation` is set (**q-lint: Set Process Evaluation**) to `direct` or `wrapped` follows that instead. **q-lint: Toggle Unwrapped Query** changes it.

q-lint.query.timeout.markdownDescription: Seconds a query may run before it is aborted, as **q-lint: Abort Current Query** aborts it; the history records it as timed out. `0`: no limit.

q-lint.query.progress.enable.markdownDescription: Count a running query's time in the status bar, and notify the end of one that ran `#q-lint.query.notifyAfter#` seconds while the window was not focused. Off: the status bar only spins, and nothing is notified.

q-lint.query.notifyAfter.markdownDescription: Seconds a query must run for VS Code to notify you when it ends while its window is not focused, with `#q-lint.query.progress.enable#` on. `0`: never notify.

q-lint.query.placeholders.enable.markdownDescription: Ask for a value for each `{{name}}` in the code a query sends, outside strings and comments, and put it in place before the query runs. Each box starts from the value given last. `{{x}}`, `{{y}}` and `{{z}}` are q lambdas and never asked for; turn this off if your code holds others, such as `{{a}}`.

q-lint.processExplorer.excludedNamespace.markdownDescription: Namespaces the **Process Explorer** and live completion leave out, without the leading dot: a root namespace (`q`) or a nested one (`ns.sub`). The namespaces nested in them are left out with them.

q-lint.processExplorer.previewLimit.markdownDescription: Rows of a table **Preview** shows in the **q-lint: query** output.

q-lint.processExplorer.autoRefresh.markdownDescription: Read the active process again after each query, so the **Process Explorer** and live completion show what it defined. Off, they are read on connect and on **Refresh Process Explorer**.

q-lint.queryHistory.search.enable.markdownDescription: **Filter Query History** and **Export Query History**. Off: their buttons and commands are hidden, and a filter set is cleared.

q-lint.processMonitor.refreshInterval.markdownDescription: Seconds between reads of the connected process while the **Process Monitor** is shown. `0`: read on connect and on **Refresh Process Monitor** only. A read never interrupts a query: it waits, or skips its turn.

q-lint.processExplorer.functionSource.en.markdownDescription: **Open Function Source**, **Edit and Redefine** and **Redefine on Process**. Off, their commands are hidden and send nothing.

q-lint.processExplorer.findCallers.enabl.markdownDescription: **Find Callers in Process**. Off, its command is hidden and sends nothing.

q-lint.processExplorer.tableHover.enable.markdownDescription: A table row's tooltip in the **Process Explorer** asks the process for the table's `meta`, rows and memory when first shown. Off, it shows what the explorer already read.

q-lint.processExplorer.editorTableHover..markdownDescription: A hover on a table's name in a q editor asks the connected process for its `meta`, rows and memory. Off by default: it queries the process whenever the mouse rests on a table's name.

q-lint.processExplorer.liveCompletion.en.markdownDescription: While connected, complete the active process's global names, as the **Process Explorer** read them, and inside a qSQL statement the columns of its table. Nothing is sent to complete: the names are those the explorer last read. Off by default, because VS Code stops offering the words already in the file once a provider answers.

q-lint.processExplorer.tableTemplates.en.markdownDescription: **Table Templates...** on a table of the **Process Explorer**: Select first 100, `meta`, count by date (run as a query), and an insert template of typed nulls (opened in an editor, never sent). Off, its command is hidden and sends nothing.

q-lint.processExplorer.schemaDiagram.ena.markdownDescription: **Show Schema Diagram**: the connected process's tables drawn with their columns, and an arrow for each foreign key and link column. It can be saved as SVG or copied as a Mermaid diagram. Off, its commands are hidden, an open diagram is closed, and nothing is read.

q-lint.dataFiles.open.enable.markdownDescription: **Open Data File in Grid** on a `.csv`, `.tsv`, `.psv`, `.txt` or `.json` file in the Explorer: loaded through q (`0:` with a type string guessed from the first 1,000 rows, or `.j.k`) and shown in the result grid. A process on this machine reads the file by its path; one elsewhere is sent the file's lines, up to 256 KB. Off, its command is hidden and sends nothing.

q-lint.dataFiles.loadWizard.enable.markdownDescription: **Load CSV into q...**: preview a delimited file's columns with their guessed types, change any or skip it, and get the `("SFJ";enlist",")0:` load statement. It opens in an editor, and is sent only when you choose **Run**, through the read-only guard. Off, its command is hidden and sends nothing.

q-lint.processMonitor.enable.markdownDescription: The **Process Monitor** view. Off, it is hidden and reads nothing.

q-lint.hdbBrowser.enable.markdownDescription: The **HDB Browser** view. Off, it is hidden and reads nothing.

q-lint.query.tagQuery.enable.markdownDescription: **Query a Tag**: run one query on every saved and discovered process carrying a tag, each over a connection of its own, and show the answers as one table with a `process` column first; a process that fails is a row with its error.

q-lint.query.compare.enable.markdownDescription: **Compare Query Across Two Processes**: run one query on two processes, each over a connection of its own, and show the answers side by side with the cells that differ marked.

q-lint.savedQueries.enable.markdownDescription: The **Saved Queries** view: named queries kept for the workspace, run on the active connection, edited as q documents of their own, renamed and deleted. Off, the view is removed and its commands refuse; the queries are kept.

q-lint.query.watch.enable.markdownDescription: **Watch Query**: run a query on the active connection every few seconds and refresh its result in place until stopped, disconnected, or connected elsewhere. Off by default, as it sends code on its own; off, the command is hidden and refuses, and a watch running stops.

q-lint.query.watch.interval.markdownDescription: Seconds between a watched query's runs that **Watch Query** offers, with `#q-lint.query.watch.enable#` on.

q-lint.testExplorer.enable.markdownDescription: List q tests in the Testing view - the `test_*` and qUnit `testName` functions a **Run test** lens is drawn over, and k4unit CSV suites - and run them on the active connection, or a process you choose. A production process is confirmed first. Off, no test is listed, read or sent.

q-lint.liveValueHover.enable.markdownDescription: Hovering a global in a q editor shows the value it has on the connected process, as the console prints it and cut at 2,000 characters. A view is named and not evaluated, a partitioned table not printed, and a production process not asked. Off by default: it queries the process whenever the mouse rests on a global.

q-lint.undefinedNames.enable.markdownDescription: Warn on each global a q file reads that neither the workspace nor the connected process defines. The process is asked, by each name's namespace and without evaluating anything, when the file is opened, saved or brought to the front, on connect and after a query; a production process only by **Check Undefined Names on Process**. Off by default: it queries the process on its own.

q-lint.argumentSlot.enable.markdownDescription: In `f[a;b;c]`, highlight the argument the cursor is in and name the parameter it is passed as, beside it, where no parameter inlay hint already does. Asks the language server only, never a process. Off, nothing listens and nothing is drawn.

q-lint.editor.continuationIndent.enable.markdownDescription: Press Enter after a line that leaves a bracket open - `f:{[x]`, `select from t where x in (1;2` - and the new line is indented, so it continues the definition: q ends one at a line that starts at column 0. A comment line is never indented after, and nothing is outdented. Needs `editor.autoIndent` at `full` or `advanced`, its default. Off, Enter is VS Code's own.

q-lint.editor.dottedNames.enable.markdownDescription: Take a dotted q name - `.ns.util.f`, `x.y`, `.z.p` - as one word, and a number as one (`1.5`, `2024.01.02`): **Add Selection to Next Find Match** (Ctrl/Cmd+D), the highlight of a word's other occurrences, and the word completion replaces. In `x+.y` the words are `x` and `.y`. Double-click and Ctrl/Cmd+Left/Right follow `editor.wordSeparators` instead, which this does not change: `"[q]": {"editor.wordSeparators": ...}` without `.` makes them agree. Off, a word is VS Code's own.

q-lint.editor.blankLineComment.enable.markdownDescription: **Toggle Line Comment** on a blank line of a q or k file writes `/ .` and selects the `.`, so the comment typed next replaces it; toggled back, the line is blank again. VS Code alone writes a lone `/ `, which q reads as the opening of a block comment: everything below it stops running, with no error. The toggle that uncomments `//` to a lone `/` is answered the same way, with `/.`. A `/` you type yourself is left as typed, and so is the toggle with `editor.comments.insertSpace` off. Off, nothing listens and the toggle is VS Code's own.

q-lint.editor.parameterCache.enable.markdownDescription: **Toggle Parameter Cache** (`ctrl+shift+'`, and in a q editor's context menu): insert or remove the statement that makes a lambda keep its arguments as globals, and the status bar item that shows a file holds one. Edits the file only. Off, the command is hidden and refuses and the status bar item is hidden.

q-lint.query.escapeAborts.enable.markdownDescription: Press Escape in a q editor while a query runs to **Abort Current Query**. Escape still closes a suggestion list, parameter hints, a snippet, the find widget or a selection first, and does nothing new in a notebook or while no query runs. Off, Escape is VS Code's own.

q-lint.processSymbols.enable.markdownDescription: Include the names defined only on the connected process in **Go to Symbol in Workspace** (Ctrl/Cmd+T). The process is asked, by one fixed read-only lambda that lists its namespaces' names without evaluating any, only while you search, and not at all when it is tagged production. Off by default: a search then queries the process.

q-lint.idiomSnippets.enable.markdownDescription: Offer the q idiom snippets in a q editor's completion list: `aj`, `aj0`, `wj`, `wj1`, `lj`, `ij`, `uj`, a bucketed `xbar` select, the `.z` handlers (`zpg`, `zps`, `zpo`, `zpc`, `zpw`, `zts`, `zws`, `zexit`) and a TorQ process skeleton (`torq`). Off, they leave the list.

q-lint.testExplorer.coverage.enable.markdownDescription: Offer the Testing view's **Coverage** profile: the workspace's functions the process holds as their files define them are replaced there with copies that count each statement, the tests run, and every function is put back; the counts show as coverage in the editor's gutter. Only a run you start sends anything. Off, the profile is not offered.

q-lint.testExplorer.failedTests.enable.markdownDescription: Show a failed assertion's expected and actual values as a diff - a k4unit `true` row `a~b`, sent as `(a;b)` so both sides come back, or a qUnit `assertEquals` - and offer **Re-run Failed q Tests**. Off, a `true` row is sent as written and the command is hidden.

q-lint.snapshotTests.enable.markdownDescription: Snapshot tests: **Record Query Snapshot** writes a query's printed result to `__snapshots__/<name>.qsnap` beside its file, after showing it and asking; the Testing view runs each `.qsnap` file's query again and compares; **Update Snapshot** rewrites one, after asking. Off, the files are not listed and the commands are hidden.

q-lint.testStub.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Generate a test for ...** on a function's definition, and **Generate Test Stub**: a `test_` function in the style of the function's test file, added to its end (or a new `tests/test_<name>.q`) after showing it and asking. Off, the code action is not offered and the command is hidden.

q-lint.backtraceLinks.enable.markdownDescription: Make each frame of a q backtrace a link to the line that failed: in the **q-lint: query** output and other output channels, and in a terminal running q under `\e 1`. A path from another machine opens the workspace file sharing its trailing folders. Off, nothing is linked.

q-lint.logpoints.enable.markdownDescription: **Add Logpoint**: wrap a function on the active process so each call's arguments are printed there with `0N!` and the last 1000 kept, without editing its file; **Remove Logpoint**, **Remove All Logpoints** and **Show Logpoint Hits**. Adding and removing go through the read-only guard. Off, the commands are hidden and nothing is sent.

q-lint.localsAtError.enable.markdownDescription: **Capture Locals at Last Error**: run the last query that failed again, after asking, with a function of its backtrace keeping its arguments, the statement it is on and its locals, put it back, and show what was kept. Off, the command is hidden and nothing is sent.

q-lint.processExplorer.driftDetection.en.markdownDescription: **Check Drift Against Process**: compare the functions the workspace's q files define with what the connected process holds, and list those that differ. Off by default: it reads every function the workspace defines from the process. Off, its command is hidden and sends nothing.

q-lint.hotReload.enable.markdownDescription: On saving a q file, send the function definitions the save changed to its process (the file's bound one, or the active connection), after Redefine's confirmation. Only a function the process holds as the file had it before the edit is replaced. Off by default: it sends code to a process on save. Off, nothing listens and nothing is sent.

q-lint.results.plots.enable.markdownDescription: Keep every chart the result panel draws in the **q Plots** view, beside q Results, to step back through and save as SVG or PNG. Off, the view is hidden, the plots kept are dropped and no more are kept.

q-lint.temporalHover.enable.markdownDescription: On hovering a q temporal literal (`2024.01.02D03:04:05`, `2024.01.02`, `0D01:00`, `09:30:00.000`, `0Np` ...) or a number of 9 digits or more in a q editor, show it converted: the integer under it, a timestamp, a date, Unix seconds to nanoseconds, ISO 8601. Also offers **q-lint: Convert Temporal Value**. Computed in the editor: nothing is sent.

q-lint.pasteTable.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **q-lint: Paste Spreadsheet Data as q Table**: CSV or TSV on the clipboard pasted as a `([] ...)` literal, each column's type inferred.

q-lint.jsonConversion.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **q-lint: Paste JSON as q** (the clipboard's JSON as the value `.j.k` reads from it) and **q-lint: Copy Value as JSON** (an expression's value on the connected process, as `.j.j` writes it).

q-lint.helpPages.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **q-lint: Show Help for q Builtin**: a page for one of q's builtins with its syntax, examples and related builtins. Works offline.

q-lint.tryExamples.enable.markdownDescription: Show a builtin's examples in its hover, each with a **Try it** link that runs it on the connected process, and offer Try it on its help page. An example is sent only when Try it is clicked.

q-lint.cheatSheet.enable.markdownDescription: Show the **q Cheat Sheet** view: iterators, joins, temporal casts and attributes, each inserted at the cursor in one click.

q-lint.query.lineTimings.enable.markdownDescription: **Time Lines on Process**: run the selection, or the file, one statement at a time on the connected process, and show each statement's time (by `.z.p`) and memory (by `\ts`) after its last line. Sends code only when the command is run, through the read-only guard. Off, the command is hidden and refuses, and the timings are cleared.

q-lint.query.functionProfile.enable.markdownDescription: **Profile Functions on Process**: run the selection, or the statement at the cursor, with every function of a namespace timed, and show them as a sortable table and a flame chart. The functions are replaced by timing wrappers for the run and put back after; the read-only guard asks first on a guarded process. Off, the command is hidden and refuses.

q-lint.problemsDashboard.enable.markdownDescription: **Show Problems Dashboard**: a workspace folder's findings, as `qlinter` reports them, by rule and by folder, with their count over commits. Nothing is sent to a q process. Off, the commands are hidden and refuse, and the dashboard closes.

q-lint.terminal.qBinary.markdownDescription: The q binary **Run Code from Terminal**, **Start q REPL** and **Send ... to Terminal** start: a name on `PATH` or a path, where a leading `~` is your home directory. It is quoted for the terminal's shell, so it is one program, not a command line with arguments. Read for the file's workspace folder.

q-lint.terminal.envPath.markdownDescription: A file of `NAME=value` lines set for q in a q terminal (**Run Code from Terminal**, **Start q REPL**, **Send ... to Terminal**), such as `QHOME` and `QLIC`, set on the command line that starts it, so they win over the shell's startup files: any value but `QHOME`, `QLIC` and `QINIT` from a copy in the terminal's environment, so it is not shown. Relative to the workspace folder, which may set its own; a leading `~` is your home directory. Values are taken as written: `$HOME` is not expanded.

q-lint.terminal.runWithArguments.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Run File with Arguments...**: pick an argument set saved for the file, or type a new one - the words after the file, which q reads as `.z.x`, and lines typed into q's console once it starts - and the file runs in its q terminal as **Run Code from Terminal** runs it. Sets are kept per workspace, the last ten for each file. Off: the command is hidden and refuses.

q-lint.discovery.refreshInterval.markdownDescription: Minutes between fetches of every discovery server's process list, at most 1440. `0` fetches only on **Reload Discovery Server**, and when a server is added or edited.

q-lint.notebook.rowLimit.markdownDescription: The most rows of a table a notebook's `@grid` or `@chart` cell is sent; the process cuts it. `0`: every row. **q-lint: Set Notebook Row Limit** changes it.

enumDescriptions: Show a larger table's first rows.
Show a larger table's last rows, such as the latest of a table in time order.
q-lint.notebook.rowLimitFrom.markdownDescription: Which rows of a table larger than `#q-lint.notebook.rowLimit#` a notebook cell shows: its first or its last.

q-lint.notebook.variables.enable.markdownDescription: Show the **Notebook Variables** view: the globals on the process a q notebook's cells ran on, read with one lambda that defines nothing, only after a cell runs or on Refresh, and only while the view is open. Off, the view is removed and nothing is read.

q-lint.notebook.parameters.enable.markdownDescription: Turn on **q-lint: Run Notebook with Parameters** and the `/ @parameters` cell directive. Off, the command is hidden and refuses, and a cell with `/ @parameters` is not run. The shell's `node out/qnbrun.js` does not read VS Code's settings.

q-lint.notebook.export.enable.markdownDescription: Turn on **Export Notebook as HTML**, **Export Notebook as Jupyter Notebook** and **Import Jupyter Notebook as q Notebook**. Off, they are hidden and refuse. Export Notebook as q Script is not affected.

q-lint.notebook.liveValues.enable.markdownDescription: Read the `{{q: expr}}` live values of a q notebook's Markdown cells on the process. They are read only when you run the code cell above them, never on their own. Off, no expression is sent; values a run kept before still show.

q-lint.notebook.processDirective.enable.markdownDescription: Honour the `/ @process <label>` cell directive, which connects to that process before the cell runs (a production process is confirmed first). Off, a cell with it is not run, and nothing is sent.

q-lint.notebook.diff.enable.markdownDescription: Turn on **q-lint: Compare Notebook Cells**, a diff of a q notebook's cells against the last commit or another notebook that leaves outputs, run numbers and metadata out. It sends nothing to any process. Off, the command is hidden and refuses.

q-lint.notebook.restartRunAll.enable.markdownDescription: Turn on **q-lint: Restart Notebook Process and Run All**: the process a q notebook's cells ran on is restarted, when q-lint started it, and every q cell runs on it from 1. It acts only when you run it, and asks first; a process q-lint did not start is never restarted. Off, the command is hidden and refuses, and nothing is sent or restarted.

q-lint.notebook.stripOutputs.enable.markdownDescription: Turn on **q-lint: Clear Notebook Outputs** and **q-lint: Set Up Git to Strip Notebook Outputs**, which installs a git clean filter for `*.qnb` in one repository after showing what it writes. Each acts only when you run it and asks first. Off, both are hidden and refuse; a filter already set up keeps working, since git runs it, not VS Code.

q-lint.agent.queryTimeout.markdownDescription: Seconds a query run by an agent through the **Run q Query** tool may take. A query that takes longer is aborted, as **Abort Current Query** aborts one, and the agent is told it timed out. `0` sets no limit.

q-lint.agent.queryTool.enable.markdownDescription: The **Run q Query** language-model tool (`#qQuery`): runs q code an agent wrote on a q process, after you confirm each call, past the read-only guard. Off, the tool is unregistered and a call already on its way is refused.

q-lint.agent.schemaTool.enable.markdownDescription: The **List q Tables** language-model tool (`#qTables`): the connected process's tables, or one table's schema, read as the Process Explorer reads them. Off, the tool is unregistered.

q-lint.agent.lintTool.enable.markdownDescription: The **Lint q Code** language-model tool (`#qLint`): qlinter's findings on q code an agent gives it. Off, the tool is unregistered.

q-lint.chat.participant.enable.markdownDescription: The **@q** chat participant, which explains q code or a q error with the language server's and the connected process's help. Off, it is removed from the chat.

q-lint.chat.englishToQsql.enable.markdownDescription: **Draft qSQL from a Description**: a language model drafts a query from your words, shown in a new editor for you to review; it runs only if you choose Run. Off, the command is hidden and refuses.

additionalProperties.patternErrorMessage: A theme colour id, such as charts.purple.

q-lint.processes.tagColors.markdownDescription: The colour of each tag in the Processes view, as a theme colour id: `{"eu": "charts.purple"}`. Over the built-in colours (`prod` red, `uat` blue, `dev` green); a process takes its most cautious tag's colour. **Edit Tag Color** on a tag row writes it.

q-lint.processes.readOnlyGuard.enable.markdownDescription: Before code is sent to a process carrying a tag `#q-lint.processes.readOnlyGuard.tags#` names, read it, and when it would assign a global, delete or update a table in place, write a file or run a system command, ask first. It holds for queries, Query a Tag, Compare Query, saved and watched queries, notebook cells, Redefine on Process and connect scripts; an agent's query that would change such a process is refused. It reads the code's text, so it is a check against a slip, not a permission system.

q-lint.processes.readOnlyGuard.tags.markdownDescription: The tags whose processes `#q-lint.processes.readOnlyGuard.enable#` guards, ignoring case. An empty list guards none. A tag is read as a process's tags are: one with a blank or a comma in it is a tag for each word, so `live desk` guards a process tagged `live` and one tagged `desk`.

q-lint.processes.readOnlyGuard.enforce.markdownDescription: Send code that `#q-lint.processes.readOnlyGuard.enable#` reads as read-only to a guarded process so the process evaluates it under `reval`, q's read-only evaluation: a write the guard missed is then refused by q - `'noupdate`, `'access`, `'sys` - instead of made. A read q refuses (a function that caches into a global, `system "pwd"`, the first `.Q.ind` on a partitioned table) is asked about, and sent again as it is only when confirmed; code the guard asked about and you confirmed is sent as it is. Not on a TorQ gateway, whose `.gw.syncexec` changes the gateway itself, nor in direct evaluation (unwrapped), nor on a process without `reval`, which is said once: the guard alone holds there. `reval` does not stop a breakpoint (`.Q.bs`, `-104!`) patching a function in place, which the guard asks about.

q-lint.connection.connectScript.enable.markdownDescription: Run a process's connect script (**Set Connect Script**) on every connect. Off: no script runs, and **Set Connect Script** is hidden; the scripts stay in the process list.

q-lint.connection.heartbeat.enable.markdownDescription: Send a heartbeat on the active connection every `#q-lint.connection.heartbeatInterval#` seconds: a `::` sent as a plain string, whose round trip the status bar shows (`q: rdb 3 ms`). One the process has not answered for 5 seconds shows as `no answer`. It is skipped while a query runs. Off by default: a process that logs its clients sees every heartbeat.

q-lint.connection.autoReconnect.enable.markdownDescription: Reconnect when the process or the network drops the connection, waiting 1, 2, 4... seconds (at most 30) before each try, up to `#q-lint.connection.reconnectAttempts#` tries. The process's connect script runs again. **Disconnect**, or connecting to another process, stops it; a connection you closed is never reopened.

q-lint.connection.reconnectAttempts.markdownDescription: How many times `#q-lint.connection.autoReconnect.enable#` tries before it gives up.

q-lint.connection.sshTunnel.enable.markdownDescription: Reach a process that names an SSH jump host (**Set SSH Tunnel**) through a tunnel the system `ssh` opens (`ssh -N -L`), with your agent and `~/.ssh/config`; it never asks for or keeps a password. Off: **Set SSH Tunnel** is hidden, a connection through a tunnel closes, and such a process is not connected to; the jump hosts stay in the process list.

q-lint.connection.torqGateway.enable.markdownDescription: Send a query to a process marked as a TorQ gateway (**Set Gateway Server Types**) as `.gw.syncexec[query;servertypes]`: to the server types a `/ @servertypes rdb hdb` line in the file names, else the process's own; **Query Gateway on Server Types...** asks for them. Off: queries go to a gateway as written, and both commands are hidden.

q-lint.tickerplant.stream.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Stream Tickerplant Table**: subscribe to a table with `.u.sub` on a connection of its own, and show its updates live in a grid. Off by default: a subscriber is a load on a tickerplant, which sends it every update. Off: the command is hidden and refuses, and every open stream closes, unsubscribing.

q-lint.tickerplant.stream.rows.markdownDescription: The newest rows a stream's grid keeps, with `#q-lint.tickerplant.stream.enable#` on. Read when a stream starts.

q-lint.processes.launcher.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Start Process**, **Stop Process** and **Set Launch Definition**: start a local q or TorQ process from its launch definition (program, script, arguments; `-p` is the process's port), with its output in an output channel of its own. Only a process you gave a definition and asked to start is started, and what was started is stopped when VS Code closes. Off: the commands are hidden and refuse, and what was started is stopped.

q-lint.processes.shared.enable.markdownDescription: Read and watch the workspace's `.qlint/processes.json`, a process list committed with the code, and list its processes beside the saved ones; **Add to Shared Process List** writes a saved process there, never its password. A password or secret in the file is ignored and said. Connect scripts, SSH jump hosts and launch definitions in it are read only in a trusted workspace. Off: the file is not read, its group is removed, and the command is hidden.

q-lint.processes.newQuery.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **New Query for Process**, in the palette and on a process in the Processes view: an untitled q editor whose queries go to that process, whatever is connected (as **Choose Connection for File** binds a file). Nothing is sent until you run a query from it. Off: the command is hidden and refuses.

q-lint.processes.logViewer.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Open Log File...** (palette, and on a `.log` file in the Explorer): a q or TorQ log in a read-only editor, coloured by level, filtered by level, process, time and text, and followed as the file grows. TorQ's `time|host|proctype|proc|LEVEL|id|message` lines, its `-jsonlogs` and usage logs, and plain q output (`'type` errors and their backtraces, a timestamp and a level word near the start of a line) are read. Files are read a piece at a time, never whole, and nothing is sent to any process. Off: the commands are hidden and refuse, and open views stop following.

q-lint.processes.logViewer.maxLines.markdownDescription: The most entries a log view keeps: the last ones that pass its filter. A new filter reads the files again, so an older entry it lets through is found.

q-lint.interpreter.enable.markdownDescription: **Select q Interpreter** and the status bar item beside a q editor that shows the q this workspace starts. The picker lists the q binaries found in `~/.kx` (KDB-X), `QHOME` (or `~/q`), `PATH` and the workspace folders, starts each once with `-q` to show its version, and sets the one picked as the workspace's `q-lint.terminal.qBinary`. A binary in a kdb+ or KDB-X install is started with that install's `QHOME` (and `QLIC`). Off, the command and the item are hidden, and no q is started.

q-lint.licence.expiryWarning.enable.markdownDescription: Warn, once a day, when the licence of the q this workspace starts is within `q-lint.licence.warningDays` of its expiry date, and offer **Check q Licence Expiry**. The date is the one q reports in `.z.l`, learnt when the picker or that command starts it, and kept on this machine: the licence file is never read or sent anywhere. Off, nothing warns and the command is hidden.

q-lint.licence.warningDays.markdownDescription: How many days before the licence's expiry date `q-lint.licence.expiryWarning.enable` starts warning; `0` warns only on the day and after.

q-lint.env.enable.markdownDescription: Give the variables of the workspace folder's `q-lint.env.file` to every q the extension starts on this machine: the q terminals and REPL, processes started from the Processes view, and q tasks. They go in the environment, never on a command line, and no value is ever shown or logged. Off, the file is not read.

q-lint.env.file.markdownDescription: The `.env` file `q-lint.env.enable` reads: `NAME=value` lines, `#` comments, an optional `export `, quotes dropped and nothing expanded, as `q-lint.terminal.envPath` reads its file. Relative to the workspace folder; a leading `~` is your home directory. A missing file is no file.

q-lint.devContainer.enable.markdownDescription: **Add q Dev Container Configuration**: shows a `.devcontainer/` for Dev Containers and Codespaces that installs KDB-X, and writes it into the workspace folder only when you choose **Write**, never over a file already there. Off, the command is hidden and refuses.

q-lint.tasks.enable.markdownDescription: The `q` task type: **run current file** and a **test** task per test runner script (`run_tests.q` and the like) under **Run Task**, and `q` tasks in `tasks.json`. Each runs `q-lint.terminal.qBinary` on its script, which exits when the script ends; the `$q` problem matcher puts q's error, with its file and line, in Problems. Off, the provider is unregistered and no task runs.

q-lint.cells.enable.markdownDescription: Code cells: a line starting `/ %%` at column 0 starts a cell, as `# %%` does in a Python file. **Run Cell** (Ctrl+Enter in a file with cells), **Run All Cells** and **Open Interactive Window**; a cell runs on the file's process and its answer lands in the **q Interactive** window. Off: the commands are hidden and refuse, and the window closes.

q-lint.cells.codeLens.enable.markdownDescription: Show **Run Cell**, **Run Above** and **Run Below** over each `/ %%` line, and offer **Run Cells Above** and **Run Cell and Below**. Needs `#q-lint.cells.enable#`.

q-lint.smartSend.enable.markdownDescription: **Smart Send** on Shift+Enter in a q editor: send the statement at the cursor (or the selection) and move the cursor to the next statement. Off by default, since it takes Shift+Enter and sends code on a keypress.

enumDescriptions: As **Query Current Block** does: the result output or panel, and Query History.
The q terminal, as **Send Current Block to Terminal** does.

q-lint.repl.enable.markdownDescription: **Open q REPL Pane**: a console beside the editor on the connected process, with multiline input, history (Up, Down, Ctrl+R) and Tab completion from q's words, the workspace and the process. Off: the command is hidden and refuses, and the pane closes.

q-lint.view.enable.markdownDescription: Open what `.qlint.view t` (the grid) and `.qlint.plot t` (a chart) send from code you run, and offer **Define .qlint.view and .qlint.plot on Process**, which defines them there. Off: nothing is defined and a call only gives its value back.

q-lint.view.defineOnConnect.markdownDescription: Define `.qlint.view` and `.qlint.plot` on each process as it is connected to. Never on a process the read-only guard guards. Needs `#q-lint.view.enable#`.

q-lint.hdbBrowser.columnManager.enable.markdownDescription: **Manage HDB Column...**: add, delete, rename or cast a column, or set its attribute, in every partition of a partitioned or splayed table on disk. The q script opens for review and runs only when you choose **Run**; a process the read-only guard guards is refused. Off, the command is hidden and refuses.

q-lint.databaseDocumenter.enable.markdownDescription: **Document Database**: the connected process's tables (columns, types, attributes, keys, foreign keys, partitions, rows) and functions, with their qDoc from the workspace, as a Markdown or HTML document. Reads only. Off, the command is hidden and refuses.

q-lint.hdbBrowser.partitionCheck.enable.markdownDescription: **Check Partition Consistency**: missing dates, tables, `.d` and column files, columns and types that differ between partitions, symbol enumeration problems and row-count outliers, as a report. Reads only. Off, the command is hidden and refuses.

q-lint.hdbBrowser.symInspector.enable.markdownDescription: **Inspect Sym File**: the sym file's size and count, the columns that use most of it, and its growth across partitions. Reads only. Off, the command is hidden and refuses.

q-lint.hdbBrowser.symInspector.warnAbove.markdownDescription: **Inspect Sym File** warns when the sym file holds more symbols than this.

q-lint.processExplorer.attributeAdvisor..markdownDescription: **Advise Attributes**: for each column of a table, whether `s#`, `u#`, `p#` or `g#` would help, why and about what it costs, from a sample of its rows and the columns your saved and recent queries filter on. Never applies one. Off, the command is hidden and refuses.

q-lint.schemaMigration.enable.markdownDescription: **Write Schema Migration...**: compare two tables' metas, on one process or two, and write the q that turns the first into the second, for review. Runs nothing. Off, the command is hidden and refuses.

q-lint.testDataGenerator.enable.markdownDescription: **Generate Test Data...**: random rows shaped as a table's meta, as q code to run locally or as CSV. Off, the command is hidden and refuses.

q-lint.tickerplantLog.enable.markdownDescription: **Open Tickerplant Log...**: read a tickerplant log in a q of its own, list, filter and step through its messages, and replay a range into that q only. Off, the command is hidden and refuses, and an open log's panel and q are closed.

q-lint.dashboards.enable.markdownDescription: **Open Dashboard...** and **Add to Dashboard...**: a panel of saved queries shown as tables or charts, each refreshed on its own interval only if you give it one. Read-only queries only. Off, the commands are hidden and refuse, the panel closes and every refresh stops.

q-lint.charts.commandLine.enable.markdownDescription: **Render Chart from CSV or JSON File...**: draw a table file as an SVG chart, as `node out/chartcli.js` does from a shell. Off, the command is hidden and refuses; the command-line script is yours to run or not.

q-lint.processes.bulkAdd.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Add Many Processes**, on the Processes view's title bar and in the palette: a form to paste `host:port[:label[:tags]]` lines or CSV into, which checks each line, shows duplicates, and adds the processes. Never reads a password. Off: the command is hidden and refuses, and an open form closes.

q-lint.processes.importOther.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Import Servers from qStudio...** and **Import Connections from KX Extension...**, on the Processes view's title menu and in the palette: they read qStudio's server list (its Copy Server List text, its XML, or its preferences file) or the KX kdb extension's `kdb.servers` or export file, and add the kdb processes named, after asking. A password is never imported, and a label already saved is kept. Off: the commands are hidden and refuse.

q-lint.connection.credentialCommand.enab.markdownDescription: Offer **Set Credential Command**, on a saved process: a command run in a shell at each connect whose output (a JSON object with `password` or `token` and optionally `user`, or a line: the password, or `user:password`) is the handshake's user and password - for Kerberos, a vault or a token service. What it prints is used for that connect only: never stored, logged or put in settings. Read from a shared list only in a trusted workspace. Off: the command is hidden and refuses, and processes connect with their stored password.

q-lint.processes.environmentColor.enable.markdownDescription: While the connected process carries a tag `q-lint.processes.environmentColor.colors` colours (production red and `uat` amber by default), show a status bar item in that colour naming the tag, and a border of it down the left of each q editor. Nothing is written to your settings and nothing is sent to the process. Off (the default): neither is drawn.

q-lint.processes.environmentColor.colors.markdownDescription: The environment colour of each tag: `red`, `amber`, `yellow`, `purple`, `blue`, `green` or `#rrggbb`. A process with tags of two colours takes the most cautious, in that order. Only red, amber and yellow colour the status bar item's background (VS Code allows only those two backgrounds); the rest colour its text. Used while `q-lint.processes.environmentColor.enable` is on.

q-lint.query.processTimeout.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Set Process Timeout**, on a saved process: seconds a query on it may run before its connection is dropped and you are told, over `q-lint.query.timeout`. Off: the command is hidden and refuses, and `q-lint.query.timeout` applies to every process.

q-lint.query.cancelLocal.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Interrupt Query on Local Process**: for a connected process started from the Processes view (**Start Process**), send it SIGINT, so q stops the running query with `'stop` and the connection stays. Off: the command is hidden and refuses.

q-lint.query.async.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Run Query Asynchronously**, in a q editor's context menu and the palette: the selection or statement at the cursor is sent as an async message, the connection stays free for other queries, and the result opens in the result panel when the process sends it back. Read by the read-only guard first. **Show Pending Async Queries** lists those still to answer. Off: the commands are hidden and refuse, and pending results are dropped.

q-lint.query.links.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Copy Query Link**, in a q editor's context menu and the palette: a `vscode://` link to the selection or statement at the cursor, aimed at a process by its label, and open such links: the query opens in a new q editor bound to your process of that label, and runs only if you say so, through the read-only guard. Off: the command is hidden and refuses, and links are not opened.

q-lint.export.schedule.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Add Scheduled Export** and **Manage Scheduled Exports**, and run each schedule when due while VS Code is open: a saved query run on a process on a connection of its own, its result written to CSV, Parquet or Excel at the file chosen, replaced or written anew each run as chosen. Only a read-only query with no placeholders is run. Off (the default): no timer runs, nothing is sent, and the commands are hidden and refuse.

q-lint.connectedClients.enable.markdownDescription: Show the **Connected Clients** view: the connected process's open handles (`.z.W`) with what is queued on each, the kind of socket, and - where TorQ's `.clients` records them - user and host, read by a fixed read-only lambda. **Close Client Handle** asks first, and is refused on a process the read-only guard guards. Off: the view and its commands are hidden, and nothing is read.

q-lint.timers.enable.markdownDescription: Show the **Timers** view: the connected process's `\t` interval and `.z.ts`, and TorQ's `.timer.timer` jobs with their period and next run, read by a fixed read-only lambda. **Turn Timer On/Off** and **Set Timer Interval** go through the read-only guard. Off: the view and its commands are hidden, and nothing is read.

q-lint.tickerplant.subscribers.enable.markdownDescription: Show the **Tickerplant Subscribers** view: the connected tickerplant's `.u.w` by table, each subscriber's handle, host (where the process records one) and output queue, read only when **Refresh** is pressed. Off, the view is gone and nothing is read.

q-lint.processes.systemSettings.enable.markdownDescription: Show the **System Settings** view: the connected process's `\c`, `\s`, `\P`, `\T`, `\g`, `\o`, `\z` and `\w`, with what each does, read when **Refresh** is pressed; **Edit Setting** changes one after asking (through the read-only guard on a guarded process). Off, the view is gone, its commands refuse and nothing is sent.

q-lint.processes.fileBrowser.enable.markdownDescription: Show the **Process Files** view and **Browse Process Files...**: the q host's directories read through the connected process (`key` on a path), and a file opened read-only, its first 1 MB only (`read1`). Off, the view is gone, its commands refuse and nothing is sent.

q-lint.processes.functionDiff.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Diff Function Across Processes** and **Diff Namespace Across Processes**: a function's definition on two processes side by side, or every function of a namespace that differs, each read over a connection of its own with a read-only lambda. Off, the commands are hidden and refuse, and nothing is sent.

q-lint.processes.findInProcesses.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Find in Processes...** and its view: search the function definitions (and, when asked, variable names) of every process with a tag; a hit opens the function's live source at the line. Each process is read over a connection of its own with a read-only lambda. Off, the view is gone, the commands refuse and nothing is sent.

q-lint.query.inlineResults.enable.markdownDescription: After **Query Current Line** or **Query Current Selection** (Ctrl+Q, Ctrl+R), show the result's short form at the end of the line, until the line is edited. It draws only what the query answered; nothing more is sent. Off, the results are cleared and nothing is drawn.

q-lint.query.benchmark.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Benchmark Expression**: time the selection (and, if given, a second expression to compare) with `\ts:N` repeated K times on the connected process, shown as a table and a chart of time and space. It runs only when the command is run, through the read-only guard. Off, the command is hidden and refuses, and the panel closes.

q-lint.query.joinAssistant.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Join Assistant...**: pick two tables (or the result on show) and get `lj`, `ij`, `uj`, `aj` or `wj` written with the keys and sorts it needs, at the cursor. The tables' shapes are read through the read-only guard. Off, the command is hidden and refuses, and nothing is sent.

q-lint.query.ajExplainer.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Explain aj Match**: for one row of the `aj` call at the cursor, show which right-hand row it matched, or why none did, by re-running the match for that row on the connected process (through the read-only guard). Off, the command is hidden and refuses, and nothing is sent.

q-lint.processes.scratchBuffer.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Open Scratch Buffer**: a q file of each process's own, kept in the extension's storage between sessions and bound to the process. It sends nothing. Off, the command is hidden and refuses.

q-lint.errorExplain.enable.markdownDescription: **q-lint: Explain q Error**: what a q error (`'type`, `'length`, `'rank`, ...) means, its likely causes and, from the backtrace of the last failed query, the operation that failed - offline, from a catalogue checked on KDB-X and PeachQ. Also a Quick Fix on a problem whose message names a q error. Off: the command is hidden and the Quick Fix withdrawn.

q-lint.deadCode.enable.markdownDescription: **q-lint: Show Dead Code Report**: the functions defined in the workspace that nothing in the workspace reads, with a link to each definition, from the language server. Off: the command is hidden.

q-lint.deadCode.checkProcess.markdownDescription: Also check the dead code report against the active process: one read-only query asks which candidates a function the process holds names. Off by default: it sends a query.

q-lint.namespaceTree.enable.markdownDescription: The **q Namespaces** view in the Explorer: every workspace definition grouped by namespace, from the language server's index, each opening its definition. Off: the view is hidden and asks nothing.

q-lint.testing.runAffectedOnSave.enable.markdownDescription: On saving a q file, run only the tests that reach the functions the save changed through the call graph, with the Test Explorer (which must be on). Off by default: it sends code to a process at every save.

q-lint.sql.enable.markdownDescription: **q-lint: New SQL Query for Process** and **q-lint: Run SQL** (the Run button in its title): a `.sql` editor bound to a process, run on KDB-X's SQL engine (`.s.e`), with completion from the tables read when it opened. Off: the commands are hidden, completion withdrawn and nothing sent.
