languageModelTools.name: q-lint_runQuery
languageModelTools.userDescription: Run a q query on the active q process, or on one named by its label, and get the result as JSON.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Runs q (kdb+) code on a q process the user has set up in the q-lint extension, and returns the result as JSON. Without `process`, the code runs on the active connection, the process the user is connected to; with `process`, a label from the user's q-lint process list (a process listed by a discovery server is `server/label`), q-lint connects to that process first and it becomes the active connection. The code is run as the process's console runs a script: each line is a statement, indented lines continue the one above, and the value of the last statement is returned. Nothing is defined on the process except what the code itself defines, so prefer queries that only read. The user confirms every call, and a query that runs longer than the user's timeout (30 s unless set) is aborted. The result is one of three JSON objects. A table, keyed table, dictionary (as columns `key` and `value`) or list (as one column `value`) gives `{columns, types, rowCount, data, keyColumns?, columnCount?, truncated?}`: `columns` the column names, `types` their q types, `rowCount` how many rows the whole result has, `data` its first 200 rows as arrays of values, `keyColumns` how many leading columns are keys, `columnCount` how many columns it has when that is more than the 100 given, and `truncated: true` when `data` holds fewer rows than `rowCount` or fewer columns than `columnCount`. In `data`, booleans and numbers are JSON values and nulls are null; temporal values (timestamps, dates, times, timespans), symbols, guids and nested values are strings as q prints them, and so are longs beyond 2^53 and infinities (`0W`, `-0w`). Any other value - an atom, a string, a function - gives `{output}`, q's console text of it. A failure gives `{error, trace?}`: q's error and its backtrace (its first 40 lines), or why nothing ran - no process connected, an unknown label (the error lists the known labels), a timeout or a cancellation. Ask for only the rows and columns needed (`select ... where ...`, `n#t`), since at most 200 rows come back.

query.description: The q code to run. Several lines run in order, as a script; the last statement's value is returned.

process.description: The label of the q process to run on, as the user's q-lint process list names it (`server/label` for a discovered one). Omit to use the active connection.

languageModelTools.name: q-lint_listTables
languageModelTools.userDescription: List the tables of the connected q process, or one table's schema.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists the tables of the q (kdb+) process the user is connected to in the q-lint extension, or gives one table's schema. It reads only, and never runs code. With `table`, the user is first asked to confirm reading that table's schema on the connected process: declined, the call is not made; and if the connected process changed after they were asked, it returns `{error}` and reads nothing, so ask again. Without `table`, it returns `{process, tables, moreTables?, namespacesNotRead?}`: each table as `{name, kind, rows, keys?, columns, columnCount?}`, `name` as a query names it (`t` or `.ns.t`), `kind` one of table, keyed or partitioned, `rows` its row count (null when it could not be counted), `columns` its first 50 column names and `columnCount` how many it has when that is more; at most 200 tables. With `table`, it returns `{process, name, kind, rows, partitions?, keys, columns, columnCount?}` from `meta`: each column `{name, type, attribute?, foreignKey?}`, `type` the q type (`long`, `symbol lists`, ...), `attribute` sorted, unique, parted or grouped. A failure gives `{error}`. It reads the connected process only: to read another, connect to it first with the Run q Query tool's `process`. Use it before writing a query, to get table and column names right.

table.description: A table's name, as q code names it (`trade` or `.ns.trade`), for its schema. Omit to list the tables.

process.description: The label of the connected process, to check it is the one meant. Omit to use the active connection.

languageModelTools.name: q-lint_lint
languageModelTools.userDescription: Lint q code with qlinter, the linter behind q-lint.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lints q (kdb+) code with qlinter, the static linter behind the q-lint extension, without running it, and returns `{findings, count}`: each finding `{line, column, code, rule, severity, message}`, lines and columns 1-based in the code given; at most the first 200, with `count` how many there are and `truncated: true` when that is more. An empty list means no rule matched, which is weaker than the code being correct. A failure gives `{error}`. qlinter reads the workspace's configuration (`.qlinter.toml`) as for the file `file`. Use it to check q code before suggesting it or running it.

file.description: The workspace-relative path of a `.q` file to lint the code as, so its configuration applies. Omit for `snippet.q`.
